A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WeEdit framework, dataset, and benchmarks. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated into v2's appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original bilingual and multilingual benchmark results, component ablations, a human preference study, and qualitative editing comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds bilingual benchmark scores produced using GPT-5.4 as an additional evaluator.

M1.justification: The glyph prediction procedure, glyph-conditioned LoRA fine-tuning, DiffusionNFT optimization, and four reward components remain unchanged. Newly specified reward weights document the existing method rather than establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 330K training pairs, 15 languages, seven training operations, and two 2,000-case benchmarks covering eight evaluation operations. The additional judge evaluates the existing bilingual benchmark without expanding task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same 15 editing baselines, and the detailed qualitative comparisons retain their six comparators. The added cross-judge table reuses existing models; GPT-5.4 is an evaluator, not a new editing baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix 7.2 adds a protocol that re-scores the bilingual benchmark with GPT-5.4 for nine systems, alongside the retained Gemini-3-Pro evaluation. Existing benchmark settings, metrics, and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a robustness check asking whether bilingual rankings depend on the evaluator, finding identical overall instruction-adherence rankings across two judges for nine systems. The original component ablations and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added judge comparison reports scores and ranking agreement without introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPT-5.4 scores in appendix Table 3, including WeEdit-RL overall IA/TC/BP of 7.39/7.51/8.46. These are additional measurements under a different evaluator, not same-setting performance changes. Tables 1–2, user-study percentages, and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same diffusion formulation, optimization objectives, reward definitions, and normalization. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: glyph-guided training, multi-objective reinforcement learning, scalable dataset construction, and multilingual benchmarks. The central claim of outperforming existing open-source models and most proprietary comparators is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 7.3 acknowledges blurring or artifacts for extremely dense or tiny text and factual or logical failures in complex reasoning tasks. Appendix 7.2 also interprets cross-judge agreement as evidence against judge-specific ranking bias; these qualifications and interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies reward weights: instruction adherence 0.3, clarity 0.3, preservation 0.15, and relative quality 0.25. V1 defines these weights symbolically without values. This improves implementation disclosure without demonstrating changed training settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds OpenGPT-4o-Image to the editing-dataset discussion and Visual Generation in the New Era to the image-generation discussion, as references 22 and 76. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized wording edits, updated affiliations, keywords, and acknowledgments. Targeted restructuring consolidates the experimental sections and moves detailed dataset statistics and qualitative discussion into Appendix 7, while retaining shorter main-text summaries.

P2.justification: The branded report layout is extensively replaced by a narrower conference layout with resized and relocated displays. Figure 1 moves before the abstract; detailed figures move into the appendix; new Figure 6 condenses existing qualitative examples; the ablation table becomes Figure 8 beside the user study; and the new judge table is added.

improvement.justification: The additional judge provides useful support for the bilingual ranking, while explicit reward weights and concrete limitations improve reproducibility and qualification of the claims. These are limited gains over unchanged primary results. Denser displays reduce readability, and the new reliability paragraph incorrectly states 9 × 8 × 3 = 243, but these defects do not outweigh the added validation and disclosure.
